claim: To give users of a self-managed AD single sign-on through AWS Managed Microsoft AD, IAM Identity Center requires a two-way trust between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and the self-managed domain; one-way trusts do not work with IAM Identity Center.
question: Which trust direction does IAM Identity Center need between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and an on-premises AD?

values.display: One-way trusts do not work with IAM Identity Center

qualifiers.scope: self-managed AD connected through AWS Managed Microsoft AD

evidence.quote: One-way trusts do not work with IAM Identity Center.
AWS IAM Identity Center requires a two-way trust so that it has permissions to read user and group information from your domain to synchronize user and group metadata.

claim: With AD Connector as the IAM Identity Center identity source, IAM Identity Center has access only to the users and groups of the single domain AD Connector attaches to, and password resets must be done in AD, not in the AWS access portal.
question: What are the limits of using AD Connector as the IAM Identity Center identity source?

values.display: the single domain to which AD Connector attaches
must be done from within AD
not be able to reset their passwords

qualifiers.scope: AD Connector as the IAM Identity Center identity source

evidence.quote: If you are connecting IAM Identity Center to an AD Connector directory, any future user password resets must be done from within AD. This means that users will not be able to reset their passwords from the AWS access portal.

If you use AD Connector to connect your Active Directory Domain Service to IAM Identity Center, IAM Identity Center only has access to the users and groups of the single domain to which AD Connector attaches.

claim: With ABAC in IAM Identity Center, user attributes from any identity source act as tags, so users who share one permission set get access only to resources with matching tags, and a change of the attribute in the corporate directory changes access without permission updates in AWS.
question: Why does ABAC with IAM Identity Center reduce the number of permission sets?

values.display: only to the AWS resources with matching tags
without requiring any permissions updates in AWS

evidence.quote: You can use IAM Identity Center to manage access to your AWS resources across multiple AWS accounts using user attributes that come from any IAM Identity Center identity source. In AWS, these attributes are called tags. Using user attributes as tags in AWS helps you simplify the process of creating fine-grained permissions in AWS and ensures that your workforce gets access only to the AWS resources with matching tags.
When Bob signs in next time, he will automatically get access to the project resources of his new team without requiring any permissions updates in AWS.
